title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: on the previous page Grothendieck defines conic neighbourhoods T of a closed subspace Y in X, with boundary Ṫ and a retraction Ṫ → Y. He also defines when such a T is (strictly) equisingular with respect to a family of closed subspaces (X_i): the induced map Ṫ_i = X_i ∩ Ṫ → Y must be locally trivial. This page (§5) states a structural Proposition that turns 'conic neighbourhood data' into 'data with a boundary'.

Category A has as objects the systems (X, Y, (X_i)_{i∈I}, T):
- X is a topological space;
- Y and the X_i are closed subspaces;
- T is a conic neighbourhood of Y compatible with the X_i, meaning T ≅ mapping cylinder of Ṫ → Y and X_i ∩ T is the sub-cylinder over X_i ∩ Ṫ.
The morphisms are isomorphisms only ('y compris les iso', apparently meaning the groupoid).

Category B has as objects the systems (X*, Ẋ, (X_i*), Y, Ẋ → Y):
- X* and Y are spaces;
- Ẋ and the X_i* are closed parts of X*;
- Ẋ → Y is a continuous map.

Claim: A ≃ B.
- Functor A → B: X* = X minus the open cone (the 'exterior' X − T°), Ẋ = Ṫ, X_i* = X_i ∩ X*, and Ẋ → Y is the link projection.
- Inverse B → A: X = X* ∪_Ẋ Cyl(Ẋ → Y), i.e. glue in the mapping cylinder of the 'link map'. This is precisely the 'déploiement' (unfolding / blow-up along Y) in the title of the notes.

Two dictionary entries follow.
1. T is a strict conic neighbourhood (one that extends slightly beyond itself, so the λT, λ∈]0,1[, are interior) iff Ẋ is a 'bord' subspace of X*, i.e. a collared boundary, compatible with the X_i*.
2. T is equisingular for (X_i) iff Ẋ → Y, together with the closed subspaces Ẋ_i = X_i ∩ Ẋ, is a simultaneously locally trivial fibration.

Purpose: this is the one-stratum step of an inductive 'dévissage'. A stratified space with a system of conic neighbourhoods is to be encoded by spaces with boundary plus link fibrations over the strata. The next page starts the induction over a finite stratification (X_i) of type I, with a boundary subspace Ẋ strictly compatible with the strata ('conification').
errors: Gap: information about X_i ∩ Y is lost when X_i meets Y outside the image of Ẋ_i → Y. For example, X_i = Y gives X_i* = ∅ and Ẋ_i = ∅. So category B must also record the traces X_i ∩ Y as closed subsets of Y, or one must impose the alternative (14) from the previous page (X_i ∩ T = ∅ or X_i ⊃ Y, with Y connected) plus a convention. As written, the equivalence is not literally correct for arbitrary X_i.

The first category is stated with 'T voisinage compatible' (the word 'tubulaire' is struck out). The equivalence requires T to be conic, i.e. homeomorphic to the mapping cylinder of Ṫ → Y with the appropriate topology. For non-locally-compact spaces, the quotient topology on the cylinder versus the 'cone' topology needs to be specified; this is not addressed.

The strictness criterion ('Ẋ a collared boundary subspace of X*') is plausible, but its proof would need care: the collar on the cylinder side is automatic, while the collar on the X* side must come from strictness.

ideas.what: Equivalence between spaces with a conic (mapping-cylinder) neighbourhood of a closed subspace and 'unfolded' data: an exterior space with boundary plus a continuous link map from the boundary to Y; reconstruction by gluing a mapping cylinder
ideas.modern_name: Unzipping / resolution of a stratified space along a stratum; mapping-cylinder neighbourhoods; link bundle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather control data (1969–70); Quinn and Hughes for mapping-cylinder/teardrop neighbourhoods (1988; c. 1999–2002); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka for unzipping of conically smooth stratified spaces (2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5: announced without proof as an equivalence between tame stratified spaces and 'dévissage' systems built from manifolds with boundary and maps between them

ideas.what: Strictness of a conic neighbourhood corresponds to the boundary Ẋ being a collared boundary subspace of X*
Equisingularity along Y is equivalent to the link map Ẋ → Y, together with the subspaces Ẋ_i, being a simultaneously locally trivial fibration
ideas.modern_name: Local triviality of the link bundle (Thom's first isotopy lemma type condition); locally cone-like / Whitney equisingularity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather; Siebenmann's locally cone-like stratified sets (1972)

missed.claim: This page is an early (1981–82), explicitly categorical form of the 'dévissage' equivalence that the Esquisse announces without proof. Here it is stated at the level of a single stratum, with the dictionary 'strict ↔ collared boundary' and 'equisingular ↔ locally trivial link fibration'. It shows the intended proof strategy: gluing mapping cylinders, then inducting over strata. This anticipates the 'unzipping' formalism of Ayala–Francis–Tanaka and Hughes' teardrop framework in a purely topological (non-smooth, non-homotopical) setting.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents the content behind the unproved Esquisse claim. It also shows that Grothendieck formulated the unfolding as an equivalence of groupoids of strict topological data, close to the modern AFT equivalence between conically smooth stratified spaces and manifolds with corners plus link bundles, but without any smoothness.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a genuine archival precursor of the Esquisse 'dévissage' equivalence, with explicit dictionary items. However, the one-step mapping-cylinder equivalence itself is essentially standard, and the general idea was publicly announced in the Esquisse.
transcription_corrections: First system: the image reads roughly '(X, Y, (X_i)_{i∈I}), T)', with a stray parenthesis.
'Ẋ et X_i*, parties fermées de X' – presumably meant to be 'de X*'.
'sous-espace bordant' is more likely 'sous-espace bord' (as on the next page).
Interlinear insertion: 'Si T voisinage cônique strict' (with 'strict' written above), followed by the struck-out 'Pour que T'; the following 'dans l'ouvert' is uncertain, possibly 'dans le sens'.
Under 'Ẋ → Y' is written '∪ (Ẋ_i)', i.e. the subspaces Ẋ_i ⊂ Ẋ.
